title: Lorentzian geometry
summary: Foundations of Lorentzian geometry at finite regularity: Lorentzian scalar products and their causal cones; Lorentzian metrics of class C^k and C^{k,α} on manifolds with corners, C^0 included; the Levi-Civita connection, curvature and geodesics of nondegenerate metrics of finite regularity, with geodesic uniqueness for C^{1,1}; time orientations, spacetimes, the time-orientation double cover and extensions; null hypersurfaces, optical functions, null generators and the characteristic hypersurfaces of the wave operator.

layers.title: Lorentzian scalar products and their causal cones

targets.name: LinearMap.BilinForm.IsLorentzian
targets.statement: For b : LinearMap.BilinForm ℝ V with V finite-dimensional, IsLorentzian b means b is symmetric, nondegenerate and sigNeg b.toQuadraticMap = 1; equivalently V has a basis in which b = −e⁰⊗e⁰ + Σ_{i≥1} e^i⊗e^i.
hypotheses: V a finite-dimensional real vector space

locator.where: §1.3, lines 296–300, p. 7; oneill1983 Ch. 2 (index)

targets.proofSketch: Sylvester: diagonalise by ±1 and count negative weights.

api.name: IsLorentzian.iff_exists_basis
api.statement: b is Lorentzian iff it is symmetric, nondegenerate and diagonal with entries −1, 1, …, 1 in some basis.

api.name: IsLorentzian.sigPos_eq
api.statement: For Lorentzian b, sigPos b.toQuadraticMap = finrank V − 1 and finrank V ≥ 1.

api.name: IsLorentzian.congr
api.statement: Being Lorentzian is invariant under linear equivalences.

api.name: IsLorentzian.smul_pos
api.statement: For c > 0, c • b is Lorentzian iff b is; for Lorentzian b, −b is Lorentzian iff finrank V = 2.

api.name: IsLorentzian.not_isOrtho_of_isTimelike
api.statement: An orthogonal family of timelike vectors has at most one member.

api.name: IsLorentzian.restrict_iff
api.statement: The restriction to a subspace W is Lorentzian iff it is nondegenerate and W contains a timelike vector.

tests.name: minkowski2_isLorentzian
tests.statement: η = −u⁰w⁰ + u¹w¹ on ℝ² has sigNeg = 1, sigPos = 1 and is Lorentzian; the Euclidean form has sigNeg = 0 and is not.

tests.name: degenerate_rejected
tests.statement: diag(−1, 0) on ℝ² is symmetric with sigNeg = 1 but degenerate, so not Lorentzian.

tests.name: index_two_rejected

tests.name: sign_flip
tests.statement: −η₄ = diag(1, −1, −1, −1) (LocalVariationalFieldTheory §3.8) has sigNeg = 3 and the same timelike set with reversed sign; in dimension 2, −η is Lorentzian and swaps timelike and spacelike.

tests.name: dimension_one
tests.statement: b(x, y) = −xy on ℝ is Lorentzian; the zero space carries no Lorentzian form.

tests.name: clifford_three_one
tests.statement: For Q = TauCeti.realCliffordForm 3 1, QuadraticMap.associated Q (half the polar form) has Gram matrix diag(1, 1, 1, −1) and is Lorentzian with timelike e₃ and value Q(e₃) = −1 at (e₃, e₃); the polar form QuadraticMap.polar Q has Gram matrix diag(2, 2, 2, −2), value −2 at (e₃, e₃).

targets.name: LinearMap.BilinForm.dualForm
targets.statement: For nondegenerate b, the inverse form on V* is b⁻¹(ξ, ζ) = ξ(b♯ ζ) with b♯ = (b.toDual hb).symm.

locator.where: §2.2, (2.2.3), lines 193–198, pp. 5–6 (contravariant metric g^♯)

api.name: dualForm_toDual_toDual
api.statement: b♭ is an isometry from b to b⁻¹: b⁻¹(b♭u, b♭w) = b(u, w); so b⁻¹ has the signature of b and is Lorentzian iff b is.

api.name: apply_toDual_symm
api.statement: b(b♯ξ, w) = ξ(w) for all w.

api.name: dualForm_smul
api.statement: (c • b)⁻¹ = c⁻¹ • b⁻¹ for c ≠ 0; the Gram matrix of b⁻¹ in a dual basis is the inverse Gram matrix.

tests.name: minkowski_inverse
tests.statement: For η on ℝ²: b♯(dt) = −e₀, b⁻¹(dt, dt) = −1, b⁻¹(dx, dx) = 1, b⁻¹(dt, dx) = 0.

tests.name: diag_minus_two
tests.statement: For diag(−2, 1): b⁻¹(e⁰, e⁰) = −½, whereas the wrong definition by the Gram matrix of b gives −2.

tests.name: double_null_inverse
tests.statement: For Gram matrix [[0, −2], [−2, 0]]: b⁻¹(e⁰, e¹) = −½ and b⁻¹(e⁰, e⁰) = 0; for 4η, b⁻¹(dt, dt) = −¼.

targets.name: LinearMap.BilinForm.IsTimelike
targets.statement: v is timelike if b v v < 0; null if b v v = 0 and v ≠ 0; causal if b v v ≤ 0 and v ≠ 0; spacelike if 0 < b v v or v = 0.

locator.where: §1.3, lines 301–306, p. 7 (null here is his 'lightlike'); sbierski2018 §2.1, lines 263–264, p. 7

api.name: trichotomy
api.statement: Exactly one of timelike, null, spacelike holds; causal is timelike or null.

api.name: isTimelike_smul
api.statement: Each predicate is invariant under v ↦ c v for c ≠ 0 and under isometries.

api.name: IsLorentzian.orthogonal_posDef
api.statement: For Lorentzian b and timelike v, v^⊥ is positive definite and V = ℝv ⊕ v^⊥.

api.name: IsLorentzian.not_isOrtho
api.statement: A timelike and a nonzero causal vector are never orthogonal; two null vectors are orthogonal iff proportional.

api.name: IsLorentzian.exists_isNull_iff
api.statement: Null vectors exist iff finrank V ≥ 2.

tests.name: minkowski_types
tests.statement: For η: η(e₀, e₀) = −1 timelike, η(e₀+e₁, e₀+e₁) = 0 null, η(e₁, e₁) = 1 spacelike.

tests.name: zero_vector
tests.statement: 0 is spacelike and neither null nor causal; null by b v v = 0 alone would make 0 causal.

tests.name: dimension_one_no_null
tests.statement: For b = −xy on ℝ every nonzero vector is timelike; no null vectors.

tests.name: null_orthogonality
tests.statement: η(e₀+e₁, e₀−e₁) = −2 ≠ 0 for non-proportional null vectors; e₀+e₁ ⊥ 2e₀+2e₁.

targets.name: LinearMap.BilinForm.timeCone
targets.statement: timeCone b v = {w | b w w < 0 ∧ b v w < 0}, the time cone of the timelike vector v.

api.name: mem_timeCone_self
api.statement: For timelike v, v ∈ timeCone b v and timeCone b (−v) = −timeCone b v.

api.name: isOpen_timeCone
api.statement: timeCone b v is open and closed under positive scalars.

api.name: IsLorentzian.timeCone_convexCone
api.statement: For Lorentzian b and timelike v, timeCone b v is closed under addition (a ConvexCone), equals timeCone b v' for v' in it, and has closure {b w w ≤ 0 ∧ b v w ≤ 0}.

tests.name: cone_membership
tests.statement: For η and v = e₀: (2, 1) ∈ timeCone (η = −3, η(e₀, ·) = −2); (−1, ½) ∈ timeCone(−e₀).

tests.name: spacelike_base_rejected
tests.statement: For v = e₁, the set contains (1, −½) and (−1, −½) but not their midpoint (0, −½): not convex.

tests.name: closure_null_rays
tests.statement: closure(timeCone η e₀) contains 0 and e₀+e₁ but not −e₀+e₁ (η(e₀, −e₀+e₁) = 1).

targets.name: LinearMap.BilinForm.IsLorentzian.timelike_eq_timeCone_union
targets.statement: For Lorentzian b and timelike v, the timelike vectors are the disjoint union of timeCone b v and timeCone b (−v), nonempty open convex cones exchanged by w ↦ −w; for w ∈ timeCone b v and timelike w', w' ∈ timeCone b v iff b w w' < 0; every causal vector lies in the closure of exactly one cone and the closures meet only in 0. Hence the timelike set has exactly two connected components.

locator.where: §2.1, (2.1.1), lines 84–98, p. 3; minguzzi2019 §1.3, lines 308–309, p. 7; minguzzi2019cone lines 236–244; oneill1983 Ch. 5

targets.proofSketch: Normalise b(v, v) = −1, decompose w = a v + w⊥ with v^⊥ Euclidean; timeCone = {a > ‖w⊥‖}; Cauchy–Schwarz in v^⊥ gives the sign of b(w, w').

api.name: LinearMap.BilinForm.IsLorentzian.mem_timeCone_iff
api.statement: For w ∈ timeCone b v and timelike w', w' ∈ timeCone b v ↔ b w w' < 0.

api.name: LinearMap.BilinForm.IsLorentzian.causal_mem_closure_timeCone
api.statement: Every causal vector lies in exactly one of closure(timeCone b v), closure(timeCone b (−v)); these meet in {0}.

targets.name: LinearMap.BilinForm.IsLorentzian.reverse_cauchy_schwarz
targets.statement: For Lorentzian b and u, w in the closure of one time cone, −b(u, w) ≥ √(−b(u,u)) √(−b(w,w)), equality iff u, w linearly dependent; reverse triangle inequality F(u + w) ≥ F(u) + F(w) for F = √(−b(·,·)) on the closed cone, with the same equality case; F is concave there.
hypotheses: u, w in the closure of one time cone

locator.where: Theorem 1.2 (lines 336–348, p. 8), Theorem 1.3 (lines 349–368, pp. 8–9), Corollary 1.4 (line 371, p. 9)

targets.name: LinearMap.BilinForm.IsLorentzian.orthogonal_isNull
targets.statement: For Lorentzian b: v timelike ⇒ v^⊥ positive definite of dimension dim V − 1; n null ⇒ n^⊥ is a hyperplane containing n, n^⊥ ∩ (n^⊥)^⊥ = ℝn, vectors of n^⊥ outside ℝn are spacelike, and the null vectors of n^⊥ are the nonzero multiples of n.

locator.where: §3, lines 176–181, p. 5; oneill1983 Ch. 5

targets.name: LinearMap.BilinForm.IsLorentzian.hyperplane_classification
targets.statement: For Lorentzian b, ξ ∈ V* ∖ 0 and W = ker ξ: b|_W positive definite ⇔ b⁻¹(ξ,ξ) < 0; b|_W Lorentzian ⇔ b⁻¹(ξ,ξ) > 0; b|_W degenerate ⇔ b⁻¹(ξ,ξ) = 0 ⇔ W contains a null vector and no timelike vector, and then W^⊥ = ℝ b♯ξ ⊆ W is the radical and the null vectors of W are exactly the nonzero elements of that radical line (§1.7), every other nonzero vector of W being spacelike.

locator.where: §3, lines 174–182, p. 5 (degenerate case); oneill1983 Ch. 5

targets.proofSketch: N = b♯ξ has W = N^⊥ and b(N, N) = b⁻¹(ξ, ξ); split by the causal type of N.

targets.name: LinearMap.BilinForm.acousticalForm
targets.statement: The associated bilinear form (QuadraticMap.associated, half the polar form) of TauCeti.realCliffordForm n 1 (time last), with value TauCeti.realCliffordForm n 1 v at (v, v), is Lorentzian with ker dt spacelike; −θ⁰⊗θ⁰ + Σθ^i⊗θ^i is Lorentzian for a basis θ of V*; the acoustical form a_{c,v} = −c²ττ' + ⟪ξ − τv, ξ' − τ'v⟫ (c > 0) is Lorentzian, a(B, B) = −c² for B = (1, v), a⁻¹ = −c⁻² B⊗B + Σ ∂_i⊗∂_i, a⁻¹(dt, dt) = −c⁻², and (τ, ξ) is causal iff nonzero with |ξ − τv| ≤ c|τ|.

locator.where: line 95; luoyu2023b lines 211–214; minguzzi2019 §1.3, lines 296–300, p. 7

tests.name: time_coordinate_last
tests.statement: TauCeti.realCliffordForm 1 1 has weights 1, −1: Q(e₁) = −1, Q(e₀) = 1, so e₁ is timelike and ker dt = ℝe₀ spacelike; time-first reading would make e₀ timelike.

tests.statement: c = 2, v = (1, 0): (1, (3, 0)) has a = −4 + 4 = 0 (null); the unshifted form gives 5 and the opposite shift ξ + τv gives 12.

s : Set F (used for sets relatively open in range I; the Lipschitz, algebra and composition facts assume s relatively open in a convex set with nonempty interior)

api.name: ContDiffLocallyHolderOn.mono_exponent
api.statement: Exponent monotonicity; implies ContDiffOn ℝ k; for s relatively open in a convex set with nonempty interior (such as range I), ContDiffOn ℝ (k+1) on s implies exponent 1 at order k.

api.name: ContDiffLocallyHolderOn.congr_cover
api.statement: Restriction to relatively open subsets and locality over covers.

api.name: ContDiffLocallyHolderOn.comp
api.statement: For s (and, for compositions, the domain t of f) relatively open in a convex set with nonempty interior: sums, bilinear compositions, composition with maps C^∞ within s, and postcomposition F ∘ f with a map F that is C^∞ on an open set containing f(s) (inversion of invertible linear maps, t ↦ 1/t on nowhere-vanishing scalar functions, exp) preserve the class.

api.name: contDiffLocallyHolderOn_iff_mem_Ckα_loc
api.statement: On open Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ the predicate is membership in PDE §1.7's C^{k,α}_loc(Ω).

api.name: ContDiffLocallyHolderOn.contDiffPointwiseHolderAt

tests.statement: The constant Minkowski form on Fin (n+1) → ℝ is a Lorentzian metric; the Euclidean form is not.

targets.name: TauCeti.Manifold.IsBilinFormOfClass
targets.statement: For ℛ : TauCeti.Manifold.MetricRegularity (C^k, k ∈ ℕ∞, or C^{k,α}), a pointwise bilinear field b is of class C^k if its section is ContMDiff of order k, and of class C^{k,α} if for every x₀ its coefficients in the chart at x₀ are ContDiffLocallyHolderOn k α on the extended chart target (extChartAt I x₀).target. The class ℛ of a function f : M → ℝ and of a section s of TM, T*M or Hom(TM, TM) is defined by the same test: C^k is ContMDiff of order k (of f, respectively of the section into the total space); C^{k,α} is ContDiffLocallyHolderOn k α of f ∘ (extChartAt I x₀).symm, respectively of z ↦ (trivializationAt _ _ x₀ ⟨y, s y⟩).2 with y = (extChartAt I x₀).symm z, on (extChartAt I x₀).target for every x₀; on an open U, the same test on the open submanifold U.

locator.where: Definition 2.1.1, lines 118–120, p. 4, and §2.2 footnote 2, lines 234–236, p. 6; minguzzi2019cone lines 81–92

api.name: IsBilinFormOfClass.mono
api.statement: Class ℛ implies class ℛ' for ℛ ⊆ ℛ'; every Lorentzian metric is C^0.

api.name: IsBilinFormOfClass.restrict
api.statement: Locality on open covers and restriction to open subsets.

api.name: IsBilinFormOfClass.add_mul_inv
api.statement: Sums of fields of class ℛ; products of a class-ℛ function with a class-ℛ function, vector field, one-form or bilinear field; quotients by a nowhere-vanishing class-ℛ function; F ∘ f for f of class ℛ and F C^∞ on an open set containing f(M); tensor products of class-ℛ one-forms; contractions b(·, X) and evaluations θ(X); and the coefficient matrix of the pointwise inverse of a nondegenerate field (in every chart) are of class ℛ.

tests.name: half_power
tests.statement: diag(−1, 1 + |x|^{3/2}) on ℝ² is C^{1,½} and not C².

tests.name: quadrant_corner
tests.statement: −(1 + (x+y)^{3/2})dx² + dy² on the quadrant is C^{1,½}, not C^{1,1} at the corner, C^∞ elsewhere.

tests.name: nonsmooth_chart
tests.statement: Through the homeomorphism (t, x) ↦ (t, x³) the flat metric has coefficient (1/9)y^{−4/3}: only charts of the smooth atlas are allowed.

tests.name: function_class_product_rule
tests.statement: On ℝ × ℝ² (self model), f(t, x) = |x|^{3/2} has derivative (3/2)|x|^{−1/2}⟪x, ·⟫, ½-Hölder (ratio 3√a/√(2a) = 3/√2 ≈ 2.1213 at x = (±a, 0)), radial second derivative (3/4)|x|^{−1/2} unbounded: f is C^{1,½}, not C². Hence f∂_{x¹} is C^{1,½} and the acoustical metric −4dt² + (dx¹ − f dt)² + (dx²)² is C^{1,½} by the product rule, not C² since g(∂_t, ∂_{x¹}) = −f.

tests.name: vector_field_by_coordinates
tests.statement: X = x∂_x on ℝ has coordinate x and is C^∞ while its length |x| is not differentiable at 0: a definition by the class of the pointwise length would reject a smooth field.

targets.name: TauCeti.Manifold.isBilinFormOfClass_iff_forall_mem_maximalAtlas
targets.statement: b is of class ℛ iff for every chart e of the maximal smooth atlas the coefficient matrix z ↦ b(De⁻¹_z ·, De⁻¹_z ·), with De⁻¹_z the derivative within range I of (e.extend I).symm at z, is C^k, respectively ContDiffLocallyHolderOn k α, on the extended chart target (e.extend I).target = I.symm ⁻¹' e.target ∩ range I ⊆ E, relatively open in range I.

targets.proofSketch: C^k: contMDiffAt_hom_bundle in every chart. C^{k,α}: transition maps are C^∞ within range I and 2.1 is stable under composition and products.

targets.name: TauCeti.Manifold.LorentzianMetric.isLocallyConstant_signature
targets.statement: A continuous field of symmetric nondegenerate forms has locally constant (sigPos, sigNeg); on preconnected M, Lorentzian at one point implies Lorentzian everywhere. For continuous X on open U, the timelike locus {g(X,X) < 0} and the nonzero-spacelike locus {g(X,X) > 0} are disjoint open subsets of U, so on a preconnected C ⊆ U where X is nowhere null and nowhere zero, X is timelike throughout or spacelike throughout. For continuous T timelike and X causal on a preconnected C, g(T, X) is nowhere zero, hence of constant sign on C. Every point has a neighbourhood with a smooth timelike vector field.
hypotheses: the field continuous as a section

locator.where: §1.7, lines 450–452, p. 11 (a coordinate field timelike at one point is timelike nearby by continuity; local timelike fields); signature constancy is Tau Ceti TauCeti.Manifold.isLocallyConstant_sigPos_sigNeg_of_continuous; constancy of causal character and time sense on preconnected sets proved here

tests.name: causal_character_strip
tests.statement: On Minkowski ℝ², X = ∂_t + x∂_x has g(X,X) = −1 + x²: timelike throughout on the connected strip {|x| < 1}; on ℝ² timelike at (0,0) and spacelike at (0,2), the null locus {|x| = 1} separating them, so 'nowhere null' is load-bearing.

tests.name: zero_locus_needed
tests.statement: X = x∂_t on ℝ² has g(X,X) = −x²: nowhere null, timelike off {x = 0} and zero (spacelike) on it, so 'nowhere zero' is load-bearing; the spacelike locus {x = 0} is not open.

tests.name: time_sense_constant
tests.statement: For T = ∂_t: g(T, ∂_t + x∂_x) = −1 on the closed strip {|x| ≤ 1} where the field is causal; g(T, x∂_t) = −x changes sign across the zero locus {x = 0}.

targets.name: TauCeti.Manifold.LorentzianMetric.pullback
targets.statement: Restriction to open subsets; pullback along smooth local diffeomorphisms; conformal rescaling e^{2φ}g; metrics from continuous coframes; the acoustical metric −c²dt² + Σ(dx^i − v^i dt)² for functions t, x^i with independent differentials (corners allowed), with B = ∂_t + v·∇ timelike, g(B,B) = −c², g⁻¹(dt,dt) = −c⁻², slices spacelike; the double null metric −2Ω²(du⊗dv + dv⊗du) + γ for a function Ω > 0 and coefficient functions γ_{AB} of class ℛ with g⁻¹(du,du) = 0, g⁻¹(du,dv) = −(2Ω²)⁻¹; and g = h − 2h(·,X)h(·,X)/h(X,X) from a Riemannian h and nowhere-vanishing X; each of the class of its data.
hypotheses: data of class ℛ (functions, vector fields, one-forms and bilinear fields in the sense of 2.3)
c > 0, Ω > 0, γ positive definite, X nowhere vanishing

tests.name: sbierski_extension_class
tests.statement: e^{2√|t|}(−dt² + dx²) on ℝ² is C^{0,½} and not C¹.

tests.name: conformal_factor_convention
tests.statement: On (ℝ², −dt² + dx²) with the constant φ = log 2, the rescaled metric e^{2φ}g has e^{2φ}g(∂_t, ∂_t) = −4, e^{2φ}g(∂_t + ∂_x, ∂_t + ∂_x) = 0 and inverse value (e^{2φ}g)⁻¹(dt, dt) = −¼; a rescaling by e^{φ} gives −2 and −½.

tests.name: pullback_direction
tests.statement: For the diffeomorphism φ(s, y) = (2s, y) of ℝ² and η = −dt² + dx², φ^*η = −4ds² + dy², so (φ^*η)(∂_s, ∂_s) = η(2∂_t, 2∂_t) = −4; the pushforward (pullback along φ⁻¹) gives −¼, and pullback along the identity returns η.

tests.name: riemannian_to_lorentzian_minkowski
tests.statement: For h = dt² + dx² on ℝ² and X = 2∂_t, h − 2h(·, X)h(·, X)/h(X, X) = dt² + dx² − 2(2dt)²/4 = −dt² + dx², the Minkowski metric; omitting the division by h(X, X) gives −7dt² + dx². For X = ∂_t + ∂_x, h(X, X) = 2 and g(X, X) = 2 − 2·2·2/2 = −2 < 0, so X is timelike.

tests.name: double_null_is_rescaled_minkowski

targets.name: TauCeti.Manifold.LorentzianMetric.covariantDerivative_nullNormal
targets.statement: For g of class C¹, ∇ Levi-Civita for g, H a null C² hypersurface and L a C¹ field on U that is a null normal along H ∩ U: ∇_L L = κL on H ∩ U with κ continuous. Over a boundaryless model, for an integral curve γ : J → U of L on an open interval meeting H, the parameter set {s ∈ J | γ(s) ∈ H} is open in J; when H ∩ U is closed in U (one defining function on U, or a level set of an optical function) it is J, so γ stays in H while in U. On intervals of the parameter set γ is a null pregeodesic and reparametrises to a null geodesic (null generator). For M Hausdorff, every p ∈ H ∩ U lies on exactly one maximal generator segment (an integral curve of L in H ∩ U through p of which every other is a restriction). For u optical of class C² and L = −grad u, ∇_L L = 0 on U.
hypotheses: L of class C¹, null normal along H ∩ U
H ∩ U closed in U (staying in H)
M Hausdorff (uniqueness of maximal generator segments)

targets.proofSketch: N = grad f: ∇_N N = ½ grad h with h = g⁻¹(df, df) vanishing on H, so dh ∝ df on H; general L via φ = g(L, Y); optical case ∇_L L = ½ grad g⁻¹(du,du) = 0. Openness of the parameter set: (f∘γ)' = df(L)∘γ with |df(L)| ≤ C|f| near H by the division lemma and Grönwall; closedness from H ∩ U closed in U; maximal segments from uniqueness of integral curves on open intervals, which needs T2Space.
